jobs.title: Vice President of Finance
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

**ELEVATE SERVICE GROUP INC.**


TSX\-V: SERV \| Toronto, Ontario

**Vice President, Finance**

**Reports To:** Chief Financial Officer

**Location:**


Burlington, Ontario (hybrid — head office based, with travel to operating subsidiary sites in the GTA, SW ON and other Canadian markets as required)

**Direct Reports:**


Controller(s), FP\&A and accounting staff — team expected to grow in line with acquisition pace

**Employment Type:**


Full\-time, permanent

**Target Base Salary: CAD $180,000 – $220,000, commensurate with experience**

**Total Target Compensation: CAD $220,000 – $290,000\+ (base \+ short\-term incentive \+ long\-term incentive)**

**About Elevate Service Group**


Elevate Service Group Inc. (TSX\-V: SERV) is a Toronto\-based, publicly listed holding company building a national platform in facilities management and essential commercial services. Elevate acquires and integrates well\-run, founder\-led businesses that provide electrical services, plumbing, equipment repair, grease trap maintenance, general repairs and renovations, preventative maintenance, and technology\-enabled facilities solutions to national retailers, restaurant chains, and property managers across Canada.


The company currently operates six subsidiaries — Infinity Group Construction, First Choice Maintenance, Charged Electric Services, Think Green Solutions, JJ\&A Mechanical, and TFI Food Equipment Solutions — and is executing a disciplined roll\-up acquisition strategy targeting three to six acquisitions per year. Elevate is currently generating approximately $25 million in EBITDA and has recently upsized a bought\-deal equity offering and secured a term sheet for a $25 million acquisition facility to accelerate this strategy. This is a high\-growth, high\-velocity environment: the finance function is being built in real time alongside the platform it supports.

**Position Summary**


Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Vice President, Finance is the senior finance executive responsible for the operational and technical backbone of the finance function across the Elevate platform. This is a hands\-on leadership role spanning financial planning \& analysis, consolidated public company reporting, treasury and credit facility management, and — critically — the financial due diligence and integration work that underpins a 3\-to\-6\-acquisition\-per\-year roll\-up strategy. The successful candidate will build repeatable processes and a scalable finance organization capable of absorbing new subsidiaries quickly and cleanly while maintaining the reporting discipline expected of a TSX Venture\-listed issuer.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Financial Planning \& Analysis / Corporate Finance**

* Own consolidated budgeting, forecasting, and long\-range financial planning across the holding company and all operating subsidiaries.
* Build and maintain financial models supporting acquisition evaluation, capital allocation decisions, and organic growth initiatives.
* Prepare monthly and quarterly management reporting packages, KPI dashboards, and variance analysis for the CEO, CFO, and Board of Directors.
* Partner with operating company presidents and general managers on budget\-to\-actual performance, margin improvement, and working capital initiatives.

**M\&A / Roll\-Up Execution \& Integration**

* Lead financial due diligence workstreams on acquisition targets, including quality of earnings analysis, working capital assessment, and normalized EBITDA calculations.
* Partner with the CFO, CEO, and external advisors on deal structuring, purchase price allocation, and closing mechanics.
* Own the post\-close financial integration playbook for each newly acquired business — chart of accounts mapping, accounting system onboarding, payroll and banking transition, and internal controls uplift.
* Track and report on acquisition synergies, integration costs, and post\-close performance against the original deal model.
* Continuously refine a repeatable, scalable acquisition\-to\-integration playbook capable of supporting three to six acquisitions per year.

**Consolidated Financial Reporting \& Public Company Compliance**

* Oversee consolidation of financial results across all operating subsidiaries under IFRS, with the subsidiary count expected to grow each year.
* Own preparation of quarterly and annual financial statements, MD\&A, and other continuous disclosure filings in coordination with the CFO, external auditors, and legal counsel.
* Ensure compliance with TSX Venture Exchange listing requirements, applicable Canadian securities law, and NI 51\-102 continuous disclosure obligations.
* Support the CFO and Audit Committee with quarterly reporting packages, technical accounting memos, and audit committee materials.
* Manage the year\-end audit process and day\-to\-day relationship with the company's external auditors.

**Treasury, Banking \& Credit Facility Management**

* Manage consolidated cash flow forecasting and working capital across the group.
* Own banking relationships and administer the company's credit facilities, including the acquisition facility, ensuring ongoing covenant compliance and timely lender reporting.
* Support capital markets activity (equity financings, debt facilities) with financial modeling, data room preparation, and lender/investor due diligence materials.

**Accounting Operations, Controls \& Systems**

* Build and scale accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls appropriate for a growing multi\-entity public company.
* Standardize the chart of accounts, month\-end close process, and reporting timelines across all operating subsidiaries.
* Lead the selection and implementation of consolidation and ERP systems to support the platform as it scales.
* Coordinate corporate tax, HST/GST, and payroll tax compliance across all entities with external tax advisors.

**Leadership \& Team Development**

* Build, lead, and mentor a growing corporate

jobs.title: AVP, Program Management and Transformation
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues \- experts in their fields \- who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients \- who are at the heart of everything we do.  



  

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.  



  

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.  



  

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.  



  

**Job Description:**

Reporting to the Vice\-President, HR Business Partner, Digital, Client Experience and Operations Transformation, the AVP, Program Management \& Transformation is a senior leadership role responsible for translating the people and workplace transformation agenda into coordinated, measurable execution across a complex portfolio of business, technology and operations teams.  



  

The role is the central orchestration point for priority people and workplace transformations. It establishes the plans, governance, management routines and cross\-functional accountability required to move work from strategy to sustained delivery, while connecting workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, employee experience, data, talent and change.  



  

This is a high\-impact role for a pragmatic executive leader who combines transformation expertise, disciplined program management, organizational judgment and strong influence without authority.  



Please note this role requires regular presence at our Toronto One York office  



  

**What will you do:**

  

*Transformation Program Leadership \& Enterprise Delivery*

  

* Lead integrated execution across the portfolio's highest\-priority workplace transformation programs, translating strategy into actionable plans with clear outcomes, ownership, milestones and value measures.
* Act as the drumbeat behind delivery, maintaining momentum week over week and proactively identifying risks, dependencies, resource constraints and decisions before they become barriers.
* Coordinate senior leaders, HRBPs, Centres of Expertise, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Data and Analytics, Technology and business workstream owners to align priorities and resolve blockers without direct authority.
* Establish fit\-for\-purpose governance, decision forums, risk registers, integrated roadmaps and escalation paths that accelerate execution while preserving appropriate people and risk considerations.

Monitor progress against strategic commitments and provide executive\-level recommendations on priorities, trade\-offs and interventions required.  

* 

  

*OKR Governance, Performance \& Measurement*

  

* Design and lead a connected OKR governance approach spanning Canadian business units, functions and HR, with clear standards, cadences, ownership and escalation mechanisms.
* Connect OKRs to the enterprise metrics agenda and performance culture, building the capability and tools leaders need to set high\-quality objectives and use data to improve performance.
* Define value measures across workstreams, integrating workforce, organizational health, employee experience and business indicators into a trusted view of delivery.

Develop executive dashboards, portfolio reviews and management routines that create transparency, surface root causes and drive timely corrective action.  

* 

*Workforce Strategy \& People Process Alignment*

  

* Lead cross\-business workforce planning grounded in labour supply and demand, capability gaps and build\-versus\-buy choices, with short\-, medium\- and long\-term talent requirements.
* Partner with HRBPs, Talent Acquisition and Finance to assess hiring pipeline health, fill\-rate risks and talent investment effectiveness, and sponsor targeted improvement initiatives.
* Align role, level, compensation and talent evaluation approaches to external technology and AI markets while maintaining enterprise consistency.

Integrate workforce transition and capability\-building plans into transformation roadmaps, connecting the work to enterprise Talent mechanisms.  

* 

*Employee Experience, Change \& Ways of Working*

  

* Embed employee experience and data and analytics into program design, using evidence to understand workforce needs, anticipate friction and improve adoption and outcomes.
* Lead the change approach for complex transformations, including stakeholder segmentation, communications, readiness, transition support and sustained adoption.
* Assess the cumulative impact of change on leaders, teams and HR, and sequence work to protect delivery capacity, employee trust and business continuity.

Advance new ways of working across the Canadian organization, simplifying how work moves across organizational boundaries and strengthening accountability, pace and collaboration.  

* 

*Executive Partnership \& Organizational Enablement*

  

* Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP HRBP and senior business and HR leaders, bringing structured problem solving, sound judgment and a clear enterprise perspective to ambiguous issues.
* Define effective connection points with Strategy and Enablement, Employee Experience, Data and Analytics, Talent and other HR capabilities so accountability is clear and work is integrated end to end.
* Prepare concise, decision\-oriented materials for the VP HRBP, CHRO, senior leadership and governance forums, translating complex work into clear implications and recommendati

jobs.description:
**Position Title:** Director, People and Culture Strategy
  
**Employment Type:** Permanent
  
**Existing Vacancy:** Yes
  
**Division/Branch:** People and Culture Division / People and Culture Strategy
  
**Application Deadline:** October 9, 2026
  
**Pay Level:** 13
  
**Pay Range:** $149,307 to $186,631
  
**Work Location:** Head Office, Toronto, ON; (In\-Office)
  
  

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an agency where innovation thrives, ideas flourish, and passion drives us to new heights of excellence. Reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General, the AGCO is responsible for regulating Ontario’s vibrant alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and private retail cannabis sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.
  
  

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is seeking a strategic, collaborative and forward\-thinking leader to serve as Director, People and Culture Strategy. Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Director People and Culture Strategy provides enterprise leadership for People and Culture strategy, transformation and modernization, with responsibility for advancing the People Strategic Plan, divisional priorities, enterprise metrics and executive reporting, HR digital enablement, responsible AI adoption, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (DI\&A), inclusive leadership and high\-performing team leadership.
  
  

This role translates enterprise and divisional priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, implementation plans, performance measures and governance mechanisms that strengthen organizational readiness, workforce planning, evidence\-based decision\-making and measurable impact across AGCO.
  
  

The ideal candidate is a trusted strategic advisor who brings strong judgment, systems thinking and a collaborative leadership style. They are comfortable operating in a complex public\-sector environment, balancing long\-term transformation with immediate operational priorities, and translating data, risk, workforce trends and stakeholder needs into practical, inclusive and measurable people strategies.
  
  

If you are motivated by the opportunity to lead strategic HR transformation, advance responsible digital and AI adoption, strengthen diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and support a strong employee experience, this role offers a meaningful platform to make a lasting enterprise\-wide contribution at AGCO.

* Lead the development, implementation and ongoing refresh of AGCO’s People Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, government mandates, workforce risks and evolving organizational needs.
* Translate organizational priorities into actionable people strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, performance measures and implementation plans.
* Oversee the planning, prioritization and delivery of People and Culture initiatives, projects and divisional priorities that advance organizational goals.
* Establish planning, governance, reporting and accountability mechanisms to monitor progress against strategic commitments and demonstrate measurable impact.
* Provide strategic advice to the CHRO, C\-Suite, senior leaders and governance committees on HR priorities, workforce implications, transformation risks and organizational readiness.
* Design and oversee enterprise People and Culture performance indicators, dashboards, workforce analytics and executive reporting to support transparency, accountability and evidence\-informed decision\-making.

* Act as a senior subject matter expert on DI\&A and accessibility, advising executives and senior leaders on inclusive talent practices, cultural transformation and emerging obligations.
* Provide leadership and direction to a team by setting clear expectations, prioritizing deliverables, supporting development and fostering a culture of inclusion, accountability, learning and high

* Post\-secondary education in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Adult Education, Strategic Planning, Leadership, Human Rights, Public Policy or a related field, or equivalent work experience; a master’s degree is considered an asset.
* Minimum of 8 years progressive leadership experience in strategic planning, organizational transformation, HR strategy, performance measurement, workforce analytics, DI\&A, accessibility, digital enablement and/or related areas.
* Demonstrated ability to translate enterprise priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, governance structures, implementation plans and measurable outcomes.
* Strong understanding of HR digital adoption, HRIS\-enabled process improvement, workflow automation, workforce analytics, digital service delivery, change management and responsible AI use.
* Knowledge of HR data governance, privacy, accessibility, security, records management and ethical use of workforce information.

jobs.title: Sr Director, Operations Finance
jobs.description:
**Department:** Finance
  
**Reports to:** Vice President, Business Finance
  
**Status:** Full\-time
  
**Location:** Hybrid/Head office (10 Carlson Court, Etobicoke)
  
Purpose
  
Gay Lea is modernizing its finance function to better support enterprise decision\-making, performance, and growth. This includes reducing manual reporting, strengthening planning processes, and leveraging improved tools and data capabilities.
  
This role is accountable for the financial performance of the manufacturing network, partnering with Operations to improve profitability through better manufacturing performance, asset utilization, and cost management.
  
The role owns costing methodology and manufacturing cost standards across the network and leads the plant controller community in delivering consistent financial visibility and performance management across all sites.
  
As a senior business partner to Operations leadership, the role converts plant and network data into operational decisions, surfaces cost and capacity trade\-offs, and shifts site finance effort from reporting to decision support.
  
  

**Key Responsibilities:**  

* Partner with Operations to improve profitability through manufacturing performance, asset utilization, and cost management
* Support manufacturing decisions through financial analysis of costs, productivity, capacity, and investments
* Develop consistent costing methodologies, BOM governance, and manufacturing cost standards across the network
* Lead financial visibility and performance management across manufacturing operations and site performance
* Own the Finance contribution to the Supply Review within Integrated Business Planning (IBP), translating capacity, utilization, cost, and inventory decisions into financial outcomes
* Evaluate operational trade\-offs and support decisions that improve both financial and operational outcomes and communicate accordingly with other stakeholders
* Monitor performance against commitments and identify risks, opportunities, and corrective actions
* Partner with Operations to improve performance measurement, processes, tools, and operational insights
* Lead, develop, and set standards for the plant controller team across the manufacturing network
* Shift finance effort from reporting to decision support by leveraging data, tools, and improved ways of working


Qualifications
  
* Bachelor’s degree in finance/accounting; CPA and/or MBA preferred
* Proven finance leadership experience in Manufacturing, Operations Finance, or Plant Controllership environments
* 10\+ years in finance with significant experience in cost accounting and multi\-site manufacturing
* Deep understanding of standard costing, BOM governance, variance analysis, and capital evaluation
* Demonstrated ability to influence operating leaders and operate at the enterprise level
* Experience leading distributed or multi\-site finance teams
* Ability to operate effectively with ambiguity and make meaningful trade\-offs
* Direct, pragmatic, and outcome\-focused leadership style
* Advanced financial, analytical, and systems capabilities


Gay Lea Foods is a Canadian, dairy farmer owned co operative with a clear purpose: to enrich life with dairy. Founded in 1958, the co operative produces high quality dairy products while creating lasting value for farming families, meaningful opportunities for employees, and positive impact in communities across Canada. As a co operative, Gay Lea Foods believes that when the business succeeds, its members, people, and communities should succeed along with it. To learn more, visit gaylea.com.
  
Gay Lea Foods is an equal\-opportunity employer and values diversity in our workplace.
  
Reasonable accommodation is available upon request throughout our recruitment and selection process.
  
Gay Lea Foods may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support aspects of the recruitment process, including screening and assessment.
  
We are currently accepting applications for this open position.
  
Thank you for your interest in Gay Lea Foods.
  
Wishing you all the best with your career search!

jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**What is the Opportunity?**


RBC's Global Payments Technology organization is modernizing international payments infrastructure across real\-time payments, cross\-border transactions, debit cards, ACH, and emerging payment channels. We're now scaling AI capabilities to enhance fraud detection, optimize payment routing, improve transaction monitoring, and drive operational efficiency across our global payments ecosystem.


We're seeking an exceptional delivery leader to orchestrate multiple large AI programs within Global Payments Technology while establishing AI\-native delivery practices that respect the security, compliance, and reliability demands of mission\-critical payments systems.


As Director, AI Delivery \& Portfolio Management – Global Payments Technology, you will lead a strategic portfolio of AI initiatives across research, engineering, platform, and business teams. You will drive alignment across complex programs, champion modern AI delivery methodologies, and ensure program management evolves to embrace AI's iterative nature while maintaining stringent operational and regulatory standards.


Reporting to the Senior Director, Program Delivery, you will own end\-to\-end delivery accountability for this strategic AI portfolio while establishing AI SDLC standards that shape how RBC delivers AI solutions for payments at scale.

 **What will you do?**

**Program \& Portfolio Leadership**

* Lead delivery on multiple concurrent AI initiatives focused on payments innovation (fraud detection, payment routing optimization, transaction monitoring, operational efficiency) with high complexity, uncertainty, and strategic value
* Manage portfolio\-level roadmaps, dependencies, and resource allocation across payments\-focused AI programs
* Own end\-to\-end delivery accountability from planning through production deployment and value realization for each initiative, ensuring seamless integration with RBC's global payments infrastructure
* Develop and maintain program roadmaps, milestones, dependency plans, and execution strategies aligned with business objectives and approved timelines, budgets, and scope
* Coordinate activities across AI Research, AI Solutions Engineering, platform teams, payments operations, governance partners, and business stakeholders across international payments, debit cards, ACH, RTR, and payment channel teams

 **Payments Domain Expertise \& AI SDLC Development**

* Maintain strong understanding of Global Payments Technology domain: international payments flows, debit card processing, ACH, Real\-Time Payments (RTR/FedNow), SWIFT, cross\-border settlement, and emerging payment channels
* Champion the evolution and operationalization of AI\-native software development lifecycle practices tailored to payments systems, where reliability, security, and regulatory compliance are non\-negotiable
* Establish standards and processes that reflect the unique characteristics of AI development in payments (model development, experimentation, data pipelines, validation, monitoring, fraud pattern evolution)
* Influence engineering teams and stakeholders toward adoption of modern AI delivery practices including continuous training, model governance, MLOps, production monitoring, and explainability requirements critical to payments
* Balance traditional delivery discipline with the iterative, experimental nature of AI development; advise teams on risk\-based approaches to AI model validation and deployment in payments contexts
* Drive knowledge sharing across programs on AI SDLC best practices, payments\-specific lessons learned, and regulatory considerations

 **Cross\-Functional Team Leadership**

* Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement across diverse technical teams (data scientists, ML engineers, platform engineers, payments domain experts, infrastructure teams, and business partners)
* Build trusted relationships across business, engineering, platform, payments operations, compliance, and governance functions; serve as the primary delivery point of contact for senior stakeholders
* Lead large cross\-functional teams and influence stakeholders across business and technology organizations within Global Payments Technology
* Coach delivery leads and team members on program management best practices tailored to AI initiatives in payments; share payments domain knowledge across delivery teams
* Work effectively with Global Payments business partners, payment network providers (networks, central banks, regulators), and third\-party payment solution providers

 **Delivery Execution \& Governance**

* Establish effective governance processes including status reviews, risk management, issue resolution, and executive reporting that account for payments\-specific compliance and operational requirements
* Monitor initiative health through delivery metrics, OKRs, KPIs, and operational dashboards; maintain performance visibility and accountability
* Identify and proactively resolve delivery bottlenecks, technical dependencies, organizational challenges, and AI\-specific risks (model performance, data quality, fairness, regulatory compliance, payment accuracy, fraud evolution)
* Anticipate and quantify tactical, operational, and strategic risks specific to payments (transaction volume spikes, regulatory changes, network disruptions); apply risk\-based approaches to forecasting and mitigation
* Manage program\-level communications including status reports, executive updates, steering committee materials, and regulatory/compliance reporting as required
* Ensure delivery teams maintain rigorous quality assurance and testing standards appropriate to mission\-critical payments systems

jobs.title: Senior Director, Enterprise Systems & AI Enablement
jobs.description:
**The Company**

 **Cineflix Media**



Cineflix creates, produces, and distributes must\-watch TV for global platforms, with operations in Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver, New York, Los Angeles, London, and Dublin. A leading international media company, the group includes top\-ranking sales and acquisitions division, Cineflix Rights, as well as production labels Buccaneer and C3 Media. With a catalogue of 7,600 hours of select programming across a wide range of genres and a collection of YouTube and FAST channels streaming 24/7, Cineflix is behind some of TV’s most popular and long\-running shows.

  


**The Role**



Cineflix Media is seeking a Senior Director, Enterprise Systems \& AI Enablement to lead the practical implementation of our enterprise AI and technology transformation agenda.



This cross\-functional role will work across the organisation to identify opportunities, modernise systems, redesign processes and embed effective AI\-enabled ways of working.

  



Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Senior Director will partner closely with IT and leaders across Cineflix to translate business priorities into practical, measurable outcomes. Initial areas of focus may include Cineflix’s finance, rights management, production budgeting, payroll and planning systems, but the scope of the role extends across the organisation. This is a full\-time role based in our Toronto, Ontario office on a hybrid, in\-office schedule.

  



The Salary range for this role is CAD $150,000 \- $200,000

  


**Key Responsibilities**

  

* Lead the implementation of Cineflix’s enterprise AI agenda across corporate and operational functions.
* Identify and prioritise practical AI and automation opportunities that improve productivity, accuracy and decision\-making.
* Translate business requirements into scalable AI\-enabled solutions and workflows.
* Lead the development and deployment of Cineflix\-owned LLM capability for internal processes, reducing reliance on external tools and ensuring solutions are tailored to Cineflix’s workflows, data, security and governance requirements.
* Establish responsible AI practices in partnership with IT, Legal, Privacy and business leaders.
* Collaborate with Creative AI leadership to align governance while maintaining clear areas of accountability.
* Develop and deliver a roadmap for modernising, connecting and, where appropriate, consolidating Cineflix’s core business systems.
* Improve the quality, accessibility and governance of enterprise data.
* Reduce reliance on manual processes, disconnected systems and uncontrolled spreadsheets.
* Lead systems integration, automation and modernisation initiatives in partnership with IT and functional leaders.
* Evaluate technology partners and solutions based on business value, security, scalability and cost.
* Lead the successful adoption of new systems, AI tools and redesigned processes.
* Partner with business leaders and HR to support communications, training and skills development.
* Help teams understand and adapt to changing roles, responsibilities and ways of working.
* Build shared ownership across functions and address barriers to adoption and measure implementation progress, employee adoption and realised business benefits.

  


**Experience and Capabilities**

  

* Senior experience in enterprise technology, AI enablement, business systems or digital transformation.
* Demonstrated success implementing practical AI, automation and workflow solutions.
* Experience leading complex, cross\-functional transformation programmes.
* Strong knowledge of enterprise systems, data governance, cybersecurity and vendor management.
* The ability to connect business needs with practical technology solutions.
* Strong stakeholder management, change leadership and communication skills.
* A collaborative, pragmatic and execution\-focused leadership style.
* Experience in media, entertainment, production or another project\-based organisation would be an asset.

  



This posting reflects an existing vacancy. Cineflix does not use artificial intelligence in the screening, assessment, or selection of applicants for this role.

  

If you are interested in this opportunity, please send your resume and cover letter to the Director, Human Resources, Mackenzie Graham via the provided link. No phone calls please. We thank all applicants, but only those selected will be contacted.

  

Cineflix Media is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing a diverse environment. Cineflix welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Business Intelligence and Analytics
jobs.description:
### **Description**

  

The Senior Director, Business Intelligence and Analytics is a senior enterprise leader responsible for building and leading GS1 Canada’s business intelligence, analytics, and market insight capability. The role gives the organization a clear, trusted, and evidence\-based view of strategic performance, subscriber growth and retention, product and service adoption, sector opportunity, and emerging market dynamics.  

The role leads a team of analysts and market intelligence professionals who measure organizational performance, identify growth opportunities, assess subscriber and sector trends, and translate data into clear recommendations for senior leadership. The function will move beyond traditional reporting toward predictive, decision\-oriented analytics that explain what is happening, why it matters, what is likely to happen next, and where action is required.  

A central mandate is to transform the analytics function through the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence. This leader will establish the roadmap, operating model, capabilities, and governance needed to embed AI into analytical workflows; improve the speed, quality, and reach of insight; and equip the team and business leaders to use AI effectively and responsibly.
  

The role translates GS1 Canada’s enterprise strategy into measurable outcomes, owns the enterprise KPI and performance framework, and ensures executives and business leaders receive timely, consistent, and decision\-ready insight. $180\-$195K


**Compensation Disclaimer:**  

The salary range listed reflects the base pay for this role at Altus Group and is provided where required by local regulations. Actual offers may differ based on experience, market conditions, and other relevant factors. The range does not include additional compensation such as bonuses, equity, benefits, or other incentives.


**Who We Need**

Reporting to the Vice President, Marketing Communications, we are hiring a Director, Brand \& Content Strategy to lead the development and execution of Altus Group’s global brand narrative and content strategy. As our new Director, Brand \& Content Strategy, you will shape how we tell the Altus story across markets, audiences, and channels, connecting our corporate brand with our product strategy, proprietary data, industry expertise, and market insights. You will set the strategic direction for brand positioning and content while remaining close to execution, guiding editorial decisions, strengthening the processes and measures behind our content ecosystem, and partnering across Product Marketing, Digital Marketing, PR, Research, Sales, and subject matter experts to deliver relevant, differentiated storytelling globally.


*This is a remote\-first role with a preference for candidates based in the Greater Toronto Area. You will work remotely with in\-person collaboration at our Toronto office as needed.*

**What’s in it for you**

*Ownership and influence.* You will have the opportunity to shape how Altus Group tells its story globally at a pivotal point in the evolution of its brand and marketing strategy. With significant ownership over brand narrative and content strategy, you will have the freedom to bring forward new ideas, establish stronger processes and measures, and influence how the function evolves. You will also help shape and develop a lean team, creating the structure and capabilities needed to deliver against the strategy.


*Visibility and partnership.* This is a highly collaborative role with exposure across the organization. You will work closely with Product Marketing, Digital Marketing, PR, Research, Sales, subject matter experts, and executive leaders, connecting product strategy, proprietary data, market insights, and corporate priorities into a cohesive global story. You will have the opportunity to influence how Altus Group shows up across markets while adapting that story for different audiences, regions, and channels.


*Creative and strategic impact.* Altus Group has been through significant transformation, creating an opportunity to rethink how brand and content contribute to the business. You will have room to challenge existing approaches, define more meaningful measures of success, and explore how shifts in search, AI, social media, and content consumption should influence the strategy. While this is a Director\-level role setting the longer\-term direction, you will remain close enough to the work to see your ideas move from strategy through execution and measure their impact.


**As our new Director of Brand and Content Strategy, you will:**

* **Shape the global brand narrative.** You will define and evolve Altus Group’s brand positioning, category narrative, value proposition, tone of voice, and messaging architecture. You will bring together corporate priorities, product strategy, proprietary data, market insights, and industry expertise to create a clear and differentiated story that can be applied consistently across global markets.
* **Lead the content strategy.** You will develop and execute an integrated global content strategy and editorial plan aligned with business priorities, campaigns, customer personas, and regional needs. You will determine where and how Altus Group’s stories should come to life across digital, social, email, multimedia, events, and emerging channels to build awareness, engagement, demand, and loyalty.
* **Turn expertise and insights into compelling stories.** You will partner with Product Marketing, Research, PR, Sales, and subject matter experts to uncover the ideas and insights that differentiate Altus Group. You will connect product and corporate storytelling, translating complex information into relevant narratives for different audiences and markets.
* **Set the standard for content** . You will provide strategic and editorial direction across content created by your team, internal contributors, and external partners. You will review and edit work with a strong eye for clarity, quality, brand consistency, and reputational risk, ensuring content reflects Altus Group’s voice and supports the broader business strategy.
* **Build a scalable content engine** . You will establish the workflows, governance, tools, and processes needed to move content effectively from idea through development, approval, production, and distribution. You will manage the content marketing budget, balance priorities and resources, and identify opportunities to improve how the team operates as the function evolves.
* **Measure and evolve the strategy.** You will define meaningful brand and content KPIs and use performance data to understand what is resonating and where the strategy needs to change. You will bring a forward\-looking perspective to evolving areas such as AI, AEO, search, social platforms, and changing content behaviours, using insights to continually strengthen performance.
* **Lead and influence** . You will lead and develop the Brand and Content team while building strong partnerships across a matrixed global organization. You will bring recommendations and strategic narratives to senior and executive leaders, create alignment across stakeholders, and help teams translate the global strategy into relevant execution across regions.

We currently have an exciting opportunity as a **Director, Data Center Strategy \& Market Development** This role is based is a hybrid in office Oakville, Ontario and reports to the Vice President, Transformation Office.  



  

Do not miss the opportunity to join a diverse group of people\-centric professionals, thought leaders, and rapid thinkers—entrepreneurs in spirit and status quo‑fighters.  



  

**Job Summary:**

  

The Director, Data Center Strategy \& Market Development – North America will lead the development and execution of IPEX’s strategy to capture the rapidly growing data center opportunity across Canada and the United States.  



  

Operating across IPEX’s traditional market segments, the Director will take an end\-to\-end view of the data center ecosystem, identifying where IPEX can create value across site infrastructure, building systems, cooling, water treatment and other emerging applications. The Director will define where IPEX should compete, develop the value proposition and portfolio roadmap required to win, and mobilize the organization behind a clear multi\-year growth plan.  



  

A critical component of the role will be developing relationships and influence with hyperscalers, colocation providers, engineering and design firms, developers, contractors, technology partners and other key decision\-makers. The Director will work to position IPEX earlier in the design and specification process and increase the adoption of IPEX solutions within data center projects.

* Develop differentiated value propositions and solution positioning for priority applications, including mission\-critical cooling and water\-management systems.
* Maintain strong awareness of emerging data center technologies and design trends, including direct liquid cooling, facility and technology cooling systems, water efficiency and evolving infrastructure requirements, and translate these into implications for IPEX.
* Lead the cross\-functional data center team, aligning Sales, Product Management, Innovation, Technical, Codes \& Standards, Marketing and Operations around common priorities and execution plans.

Measures of Success


* Clear North American data center strategy and multi\-year growth roadmap established and executed.
* Strong relationships developed with priority hyperscalers, colocation providers, engineering firms and other specification influencers.
* Increased IPEX inclusion in data center designs and specifications.
* Measurable pipeline and profitable incremental revenue generated across multiple IPEX segments.
* Priority product and capability gaps identified and addressed through innovation, partnerships or portfolio development.
* Differentiated IPEX value propositions established for priority applications, including cooling and water\-management solutions.
* Cross\-functional resources aligned around a common set of data center priorities.
